hook.line: Five in the morning at the terminal, and Hernando turns up with a bag of arepas for the road. One thank you, one question, and both little words in a single breath.
hook.es: Gracias por todo, Hernando. ¿Esto es para el viaje?
hook.en: Thanks for everything, Hernando. Is this for the trip?

examples.en: This present is for you. (to a friend)
I made it for you. (to a friend)
I did it for your sake. (to a friend)
I'll do it in the morning.

examples.es: Pasamos por Cali y seguimos para Medellín.
examples.en: We went through Cali and carried on to Medellín.

rule:
Look at the pairs above. Same sentence, one little word swapped, and the meaning turns round.

*para* points forward:
heading to a place: *para Medellín*
for someone to have: *para ti*
due by a day: *para mañana*
in order to: *para dormir*

*por* looks at the way or the cause:
through a place: *por Cali*
because of: *por la lluvia*, *por ti*
a price or a swap: *por cien mil*
per: *por noche*
and part of the day: *por la mañana*

The pair to watch is *para ti* and *por ti*. A gift is *para ti*: it ends up with you. *Por ti* means you're the reason: I did it because of you, for your sake.

A quick test: if because of, through or per fits in English, it's *por*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these two prepositions. This contrast comes back at B1, when *por* picks up more jobs.

readAndPick.es: Me quedé en Bogotá por mi abuela.
options: I stayed in Bogotá to give something to my grandmother.
I stayed in Bogotá because of my grandmother.
I bought flowers for my grandmother.
I bought flowers because of my grandmother.
We didn't go out to see the rain.
We didn't go out because of the rain.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *por* or *para* and type the whole sentence: Gracias ___ el regalo.
yourTurn.why: Thanks looks back at what someone did: *gracias por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *por* or *para* and type the whole sentence: Este regalo es ___ ti.
yourTurn.why: The present ends up with you, so *para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *por* or *para* and type the whole sentence: Lo hago ___ la mañana. (I'll do it in the morning.)
yourTurn.why: Part of the day is *por la mañana*; *para mañana* would be a deadline.
A deadline is where the arrow points: *para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: I made it for you.
yourTurn.why: It's yours to have, so *para ti*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We went through Cali and carried on to Medellín.
yourTurn.answer: Pasamos por Cali y seguimos para Medellín.
yourTurn.why: Cali is on the way (*por*); Medellín is where you're heading (*para*).

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a thank you: *Me ayudaste con la maleta.* (Thanks for helping me with the suitcase.)
yourTurn.answer: Gracias por ayudarme con la maleta.
yourTurn.why: *Gracias por* + the basic verb, with *me* glued on the end.

pitfalls.why: Almost. A present goes to you, so *para*; *por ti* would mean because of you.
By Monday is a deadline, and deadlines take *para*.
In the morning is *por la mañana*, a set phrase you already know.

personal: Think of something you did for someone. Say who it was for with *para*, and why with *por*: *Lo hice para mi hermana. Lo hice por…*
